35.0.0.en: 1 Moreover the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 "Son of man, set thy face against mount Seir, and prophesy against it, 3 And say unto it, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, O mount Seir, I am against thee, and I will stretch out mine hand against thee, and I will make thee most desolate. 4 I will lay thy cities waste, and thou shalt be desolate, and thou shalt know that I am the LORD. 5 Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end: 6 Therefore, as I live, saith the Lord GOD, I will prepare thee unto blood, and blood shall pursue thee: sith thou hast not hated blood, even blood shall pursue thee. 7 Thus will I make mount Seir most desolate, and cut off from it him that passeth out and him that returneth. 8 And I will fill his mountains with his slain men: in thy hills, and in thy valleys, and in all thy rivers, shall they fall that are slain with the sword. 9 I will make thee perpetual desolations, and thy cities shall not return: and ye shall know that I am the LORD. 10 Because thou hast said, These two nations and these two countries shall be mine, and we will possess it; whereas the LORD was there: 11 Therefore, as I live, saith the Lord GOD, I will even do according to thine anger, and according to thine envy which thou hast used out of thy hatred against them; and I will make myself known among them, when I have judged thee. 12 And thou shalt know that I am the LORD, and that I have heard all thy blasphemies which thou hast spoken against the mountains of Israel, saying, They are laid desolate, they are given us to consume. 13 Thus with your mouth ye have boasted against me, and have multiplied your words against me: I have heard them. 14 Thus saith the Lord GOD; When the whole earth rejoiceth, I will make thee desolate. 15 As thou didst rejoice at the inheritance of the house of Israel, because it was desolate, so will I do unto thee: thou shalt be desolate, O mount Seir, and all Idumea, even all of it: and they shall know that I am the LORD."

35.0.1.en: During the prophecies against the foreign nations that rejoiced at Israel's fall (Ezek 25-33), the prophet Ezekiel prophesied against Seir together with Moab (Ezek 25:8), and also prophesied against Edom, which includes mount Seir within it (Ezek 25:12). Why then did he return to prophesy at some length against Seir while speaking of the inner reformation? 1. We cannot separate the outward work from the inward work. Truly God wanted to prepare the way for the return and the inner reformation, at the level of the people and the shepherds, by tearing down the outward powers of evil; but in actual practice the two reformations are bound together. There is no tearing down of the outward powers of evil without repentance beginning within, and no reformation without the beginning of the tearing down of outward evil. Moreover, every inner reformation stirs up the outward enemy (the devil) and enrages him; therefore Nehemiah built with one hand and held the weapon in the other. So when a man works spiritually he must be watchful against every war that rises against him to destroy him. 2. Perhaps he took care to speak of mount Seir in particular because news reached the captives that the Edomites had gradually infiltrated Judah after the breaking of Jerusalem and occupied it, so the prophet wished to assure them that God would rescue the land from the hands of those who occupied it, especially since the dispute over the land between Israel and Edom was an ancient matter (Gen 27:40). In this he opened a new reason for the reformation, for God intervenes to reform on account of the slanders of the people of Seir, which appears clearly in the following chapter.

35.1.0.en: The foundations on which the prophecy against them rests are: 1. Hatred: Seir's hatred of the people was an ancient hatred rooted in the depths of their hearts, for He says: "Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end" [5]. The hatred did not stop at rejoicing in their calamity but turned into injustice and bloodshed that delivered them to the sword. She loved the ... Therefore blood pursues her, or as the Lord says: "Sith thou hast not hated blood, even blood shall pursue thee" [6].

35.2.0.en: With the measure that a man measures, it shall be measured to him, and into the pit that he digs for his brother he himself falls; the cross that Haman prepared for Mordecai, he himself was hanged on it. 2. Its seizing of others: "Because thou hast said, These two nations and these two countries shall be mine, and we will possess it; whereas the LORD was there..." [10]. Thus when a man wants to seize a land that is not his own, and to possess what is not his, he does not realize that the invisible God looks and beholds the injustice. She wanted to possess what was not hers, and therefore loses what is hers, for her cities become waste and she becomes desolate [4]. 3. Its arrogance, full of blasphemy: "Thus with your mouth ye have boasted against me, and have multiplied your words against me: I have heard them" [13]. When she wanted to possess what was not hers, the Lord was there, seeing their wickedness; and when she was arrogant in her heart and spoke with her lips against God, God was listening. He has been long-suffering for a long time, but He repays her for her blasphemy. 4. She rejoiced at the harm of Judah on the day of its chastisement: when Judah fell under chastisement she was not admonished but rejoiced in her gloating, and therefore she deserved the wrath of God: "As thou didst rejoice at the inheritance of the house of Israel, because it was desolate, so will I do unto thee: thou shalt be desolate, O mount Seir, and all Idumea, even all of it: and they shall know that I am the LORD" [15].

35.2.1.en: That is, what befell mount Seir is the fruit of its inward sin, bearing the same fruit as its deeds, and also for the building up of the people of God; for since these had usurped their rights, God defends His children for the sake of His holy name, "and they shall know that I am the LORD."

35.2.2.en: Let all Your enemies be scattered!

35.2.3.en: * Who is Seir (Edom), who gloats over Your Church, if not the violent enemy of the good, the shedder of blood?!

35.2.5.en: His hatred of me is very ancient; it is a hatred of You, O Beloved of my soul!

35.2.6.en: He hates me greatly, because he hates You!

35.2.7.en: He prepared the Cross for You, and by it he himself was crushed!

35.2.8.en: * My enemy wants to seize my heart; it is neither his nor mine, but wholly Yours!

35.2.9.en: He wants to possess what is not his, to seize Your Kingdom that is within me!

35.2.10.en: Arise, O Lord, and let all Your enemies be scattered, and let all who hate Your name flee from before Your face!

35.2.11.en: * My enemy is arrogant, but his end is in hell!

35.2.12.en: As for me, bear me by Your Holy Spirit into the bosom of Your Father!

36.0.0.en: 1 "Also, thou son of man, prophesy unto the mountains of Israel, and say, Ye mountains of Israel, hear the word of the LORD: 2 Thus saith the Lord GOD; Because the enemy hath said against you, Aha, even the ancient high places are ours in possession: 3 Therefore prophesy and say, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Because they have made you desolate, and swallowed you up on every side, that ye might be a possession unto the residue of the heathen, and ye are taken up in the lips of talkers, and are an infamy of the people: 4 Therefore, ye mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD; Thus saith the Lord GOD to the mountains, and to the hills, to the rivers, and to the valleys, to the desolate wastes, and to the cities that are forsaken, which became a prey and derision to the residue of the heathen that are round about; 5 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Surely in the fire of my jealousy have I spoken against the residue of the heathen, and against all Idumea, which have appointed my land into their possession with the joy of all their heart, with despiteful minds, to cast it out for a prey. 6 Prophesy therefore concerning the land of Israel, and say unto the mountains, and to the hills, to the rivers, and to the valleys, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I have spoken in my jealousy and in my fury, because ye have borne the shame of the heathen: 7 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; I have lifted up mine hand, Surely the heathen that are about you, they shall bear their shame. 8 But ye, O mountains of Israel, ye shall shoot forth your branches, and yield your fruit to my people of Israel; for they are at hand to come. 9 For, behold, I am for you, and I will turn unto you, and ye shall be tilled and sown: 10 And I will multiply men upon you, all the house of Israel, even all of it: and the cities shall be inhabited, and the wastes shall be builded: 11 And I will multiply upon you man and beast; and they shall increase and bring fruit: and I will settle you after your old estates, and will do better unto you than at your beginnings: and ye shall know that I am the LORD. 12 Yea, I will cause men to walk upon you, even my people Israel; and they shall possess thee, and thou shalt be their inheritance, and thou shalt no more henceforth bereave them of men. 13 Thus saith the Lord GOD; Because they say unto you, Thou land devourest up men, and hast bereaved thy nations; 14 Therefore thou shalt devour men no more, neither bereave thy nations any more, saith the Lord GOD. 15 Neither will I cause men to hear in thee the shame of the heathen any more, neither shalt thou bear the reproach of the people any more, neither shalt thou cause thy nations to fall any more, saith the Lord GOD."

36.1.0.en: In this chapter God revealed a new reason for His intervention to reform the state of His people, namely His jealousy for His holy name, which the Gentiles dishonored, thinking God weak because of the chastisements that befell His people. They gloated over the ruin of His people and insulted His holy name, and infiltrated the land of inheritance so that it might become an inheritance for them instead of the people of God, for the Lord GOD says: "Because the enemy hath said against you, Aha, even the ancient high places are ours in possession" [2]. They rejoiced in the defeat and exploited it, and therefore the Lord rose to save His people "in the fire of my jealousy" [5]. The Lord looks upon the mountains and the hills, the rivers and the valleys, the desolate wastes and the forsaken cities that became a prey and derision to the residue of the Gentiles round about, and says: "Behold, I have spoken in my jealousy and in my fury, because ye have borne the shame of the heathen: Therefore... I have lifted up mine hand, Surely the heathen that are about you, they shall bear their shame" [7].

36.1.1.en: What are these mountains if not the prophets, and the hills the priests, and the rivers the teachers, and the valleys the weak souls; and the desolate wastes and the forsaken cities are the people who perished because of their evil and the neglect of their shepherding.

36.1.2.en: He speaks with the shepherds and the flock, the priests and the people, the great and the despised, the steadfast like the mountains and the collapsed like the ruined cities... He speaks with all, declaring that He intervenes to reform them, not for the sake of any of them, but for the sake of His fiery jealousy on account of the reproaches of the Gentiles against them and against Him!

36.2.0.en: He lifted up His hand [7] to speak against the nations, as though He stood declaring an oath, for it was the custom of the Jews at that time, when they swore, to lift up their hands. He affirms with an oath that He intervenes to reform them by His burning jealousy. In this He does not wrong the nations, but repays them for their deeds, for "they shall bear their shame" [7]. What they do to others returns upon them; they drink the same cup that they prepared for others.

36.3.0.en: The Lord turns again to look upon the holy mountains, as upon His Church, declaring that He offers it a new possibility of bearing fruit, so that when His people return to it they find the mountains tilled and fruitful, the cities inhabited and the wastes builded [10], and the mountains filled with men and beasts [12].

36.4.0.en: Wonderful is God in His love for man, for He offers him the possibility of returning, not to what he was before the fall and the captivity, but to a better state, for He says: "I will settle you after your old estates, and will do better unto you than at your beginnings: and ye shall know that I am the LORD" [11]. This is what the Lord Christ did for us: He gave us the holy mountains (the Church), tilled and prepared for dwelling in them, not like the old lost Paradise but even greater. We enter the holy mountains and do not find the tree of life but Christ Himself, the Giver of life; instead of rivers we find the springs of the Holy Spirit overflowing with divine graces; and instead of the destruction and ruin that befell us, the heart is filled with the eternal Kingdom of God.

36.4.1.en: In the era of grace man did not merely return to his original state before the fall, but became a son of the Father, a member in the body of the Lord Christ and a holy temple of the Holy Spirit... What glory is greater than this?! Our state now, in Christ Jesus, has become better than what we were at our beginnings!

36.4.2.en: What does the Lord do with His holy mountain? "I will multiply men upon you... And I will multiply upon you man and beast; and they shall increase and bring fruit: and I will settle you... Yea, I will cause men to walk upon you, even my people Israel; and they shall possess thee, and thou shalt be their inheritance, and thou shalt no more henceforth bereave them of men" [10-12].

36.4.3.en: He multiplies men within His Church, His holy mountain, bringing them from the east and the west, from every nation, tongue and people. He multiplies man and beast, and they increase and bring fruit, meaning that not only does He bring them from all the world to His mountain, but He blesses each one of them: He blesses his soul (man) and his body (signified by the beast), multiplying them and making them fruitful, for the soul bears, as does the body, of the fruit of the Holy Spirit.

36.4.4.en: There is no longer enmity between man and beast, between soul and body, but they dwell together as in Paradise, in harmony, working under the leadership of the Holy Spirit.

36.4.5.en: He says that men walk upon the mountains, for they enter as the people of God into the Church, and are in a state of continual movement without stopping until they inherit the holy mountain, and death no longer draws near to them! They enter the eternal Church, the divine inheritance, where there is no death, no pain and no distress.

36.5.0.en: 16 Moreover the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 17 "Son of man, when the house of Israel dwelt in their own land, they defiled it by their own way and by their doings: their way was before me as the uncleanness of a removed woman. 18 Wherefore I poured my fury upon them for the blood that they had shed upon the land, and for their idols wherewith they had polluted it: 19 And I scattered them among the heathen, and they were dispersed through the countries: according to their way and according to their doings I judged them. 20 And when they entered unto the heathen, whither they went, they profaned my holy name, when they said to them, These are the people of the LORD, and are gone forth out of his land. 21 But I had pity for mine holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the heathen, whither they went."

36.5.1.en: It is as though the prophet asks: Since You bring the people back to a better state than they were in, so that the ruined cities are rebuilt and the ruins are built up, why did You permit the destruction and ruin? And the divine answer came, declaring that what God did was to chastise the people because of their evil, so that when they fell under chastisement and the nations reproached them, He might rise in His divine jealousy and bring them back to a better state than they were in. Their deeds before were unclean like the rag of a menstruous woman; they committed abominations and shed blood and became the cause of blasphemy against His holy name... And yet, having chastised them, He turned again and had compassion on them for the sake of His holy name.

36.6.0.en: 22 "Therefore say unto the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord GOD; I do not this for your sakes, O house of Israel, but for mine holy name's sake, which ye have profaned among the heathen, whither ye went. 23 And I will sanctify my great name, which was profaned among the heathen, which ye have profaned in the midst of them; and the heathen shall know that I am the LORD, saith the Lord GOD, when I shall be sanctified in you before their eyes. 24 For I will take you from among the heathen, and gather you out of all countries, and will bring you into your own land. 25 Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you. 26 A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh. 27 And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them. 28 And ye shall dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers; and ye shall be my people, and I will be your God. 29 I will also save you from all your uncleannesses: and I will call for the corn, and will increase it, and lay no famine upon you. 30 And I will multiply the fruit of the tree, and the increase of the field, that ye shall receive no more reproach of famine among the heathen. 31 Then shall ye remember your own evil ways, and your doings that were not good, and shall loathe yourselves in your own sight for your iniquities and for your abominations. 32 Not for your sakes do I this, saith the Lord GOD, be it known unto you: be ashamed and confounded for your own ways, O house of Israel. 33 Thus saith the Lord GOD; In the day that I shall have cleansed you from all your iniquities I will also cause you to dwell in the cities, and the wastes shall be builded. 34 And the desolate land shall be tilled, whereas it lay desolate in the sight of all that passed by. 35 And they shall say, This land that was desolate is become like the garden of Eden; and the waste and desolate and ruined cities are become fenced, and are inhabited. 36 Then the heathen that are left round about you shall know that I the LORD build the ruined places, and plant that that was desolate: I the LORD have spoken it, and I will do it. 37 Thus saith the Lord GOD; I will yet for this be enquired of by the house of Israel, to do it for them; I will increase them with men like a flock. 38 As the holy flock, as the flock of Jerusalem in her solemn feasts; so shall the waste cities be filled with flocks of men: and they shall know that I am the LORD."

36.6.1.en: Having spoken of His jealousy for reformation, he began by speaking of the aim of this reformation and then its means. Its aim is: "I do not this for your sakes, O house of Israel, but for mine holy name's sake... And I will sanctify my great name... and the heathen shall know that I am the LORD, saith the Lord GOD, when I shall be sanctified in you before their eyes" [22-23].

36.6.2.en: What does the Lord mean by this? Does He work for our salvation and reformation for the sake of His holy name and not for our sake? Is there selfishness in this? Does He love the glory of His holy name and not care for us? Impossible! In saying "not for your sakes" He does not mean that He does not care for us; rather, He does not work out of any merit in us, nor by our capacities, but works in us for His name's sake by His capacities as the Holy One. He loves us and so makes us the object of "the glorifying of His holy name," and so He is revealed in His holiness in us, like a father who rejoices in his successful children as though he himself were the successful one, and counts them worthy of his fatherhood. He lifts us from the spirit of bondage to the spirit of sonship, able to declare clearly the glory of the Father; or He raises us up as a holy body that reveals by its wise conduct the wisdom of the Head who directs it.

36.6.3.en: His concern to declare the holiness of His name in us is the very same love for us!

36.6.4.en: The means of radical reformation are:

36.7.0.en: a. "For I will take you from among the heathen, and gather you out of all countries, and will bring you into your own land" [24]. It is a call to raise up one holy people, whom He gathers out of all countries, that is, out of every nation, tongue and people, and He brings all of them into their own land, that is, into the Church which is theirs. This is the call of the Lord Christ to all mankind, to be gathered in Him to become His holy body, and to rest in Him as in their own land or house.

36.7.1.en: b. If God, because of the shedding of blood and the abominations of idolatry, appeared weak among the nations, delivering His people to Babylon, then in order that His holy name may be glorified and His power shown, what is needed is not merely their return to their land but rather the forgiveness of their sins by the precious Blood poured out for them. This is what they enjoy through the waters of holy Baptism.

36.8.0.en: "Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you" [25]. In this they obtain the forgiveness of their sins, and it is right for them to return to their cities and build their ruins: "Thus saith the Lord GOD; In the day that I shall have cleansed you from all your iniquities I will also cause you to dwell in the cities, and the wastes shall be builded. And the desolate land shall be tilled, whereas it lay desolate in the sight of all that passed by" [33-34].

36.8.1.en: This is the work of the holy waters, for St. Barnabas says: [Truly we go down into the water full of sins and defilement, and we come up bearing fruit in our hearts, bearing in our spirit the fear (of God) and the hope in Jesus]. And St. Clement of Alexandria says: [Baptism washes us from every blemish, and makes us the holy temple of God, and restores us to the communion of the divine nature by the Holy Spirit.

36.9.0.en: c. The cleansing in the holy waters does not stop at washing us from our old sins and removing every blemish in us, but extends to granting us a new nature that stands in place of the corrupt nature that we had, a nature fit for the new life in the new land: "A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh" [26]. This new heart and this new spirit are realized by our receiving the new spiritual birth in the waters of holy Baptism. St. Cyprian says: [It is the Baptism in which the old man dies and the new man is born, as the Apostle declares, affirming that He saved us by the washing of the second birth and the renewing of the Holy Spirit (Titus 3:5)].

36.10.0.en: d. By our receiving forgiveness and enjoying the new heart by the Holy Spirit within the waters of Baptism, we are prepared to receive the Holy Spirit in us in the Myron. This is the sign of the New Covenant, the gift of the Lord Christ to us, that He gave us His Spirit, for He says: "And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them" [27]. This is the new possibility of walking in the commandments of the Lord and keeping His judgments and doing them; it is the possibility of His Holy Spirit who was given to us within us. Therefore the prophets stressed this gift, and among their sayings:

36.10.1.en: "And I will put my spirit in you, and ye shall live" (Ezek 37:14).

36.10.2.en: "Neither will I hide my face any more from them: for I have poured out my spirit upon the house of Israel" (Ezek 39:26).

36.10.3.en: "For I will pour water upon him that is thirsty, and floods upon the dry ground: I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thine offspring" (Isa 44:3) (the work of the Holy Spirit in us is like the work of water in the thirsty and floods on the dry ground).

36.10.4.en: "And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions: and also upon the servants and upon the handmaids in those days will I pour out my spirit" (Joel 2:28-29).

36.11.0.en: e. Our constant remembrance of our weakness, for He says: "Then shall ye remember your own evil ways, and your doings that were not good, and shall loathe yourselves in your own sight for your iniquities and for your abominations" [31]. Although God has given us forgiveness of our sins through the merits of His Blood, and has given us a new nature and has given us His Spirit dwelling in us, yet in the midst of our joy at the great works of God with us and our continual hope in Him, we ought to remember our weaknesses as a rebuke to our souls and a warning to us lest we fall. As the repentant psalmist says: "My sin is ever before me" (Ps 51). It is as with the paralytic who was healed and rose from his bed of sickness, yet was bound to carry his bed, that he might not forget his weaknesses. However, in remembering our sins it is fitting for us to walk in a spirit of discernment, so that we do not remember our sins in their details and stumble by recalling them, nor remember them in a spirit of despair and lose our joy in salvation. St. Pinufius spoke much on this matter, warning us lest, because of remembering sins, our souls be suffocated by the stifling smell of the sewers.

36.12.0.en: f. Constant growth: through our remembrance of our own weakness we believe in Him who works in us without ceasing for our attaining perfection. Our sense of our weakness may crush our souls, but our faith in Him who works in us continually makes us grow; therefore the Lord continues, saying: "I the LORD build the ruined places, and plant that that was desolate: I the LORD have spoken it, and I will do it" [36]. He says also: "I will increase them with men like a flock. As the holy flock, as the flock of Jerusalem in her solemn feasts; so shall the waste cities be filled with flocks of men" [37-38]. He works in us to fill our inner Jerusalem with abundant fruit, and moves us from glory to glory to bring us into His perfection.

36.12.1.en: Make me a holy mountain for You!

36.12.2.en: *Make me, O Lord, a holy mountain for You!

36.12.3.en: Make me steadfast like the mountains, that the enemy of the good may not be able to move me!

36.12.4.en: *Send Your Holy Spirit upon me like rain, and turn me into a fruitful garden.

36.12.7.en: *You multiply men and beasts; bless my rational soul, and sanctify my body, that it may no longer bear an animal nature!

36.12.8.en: Your Holy Spirit renews my nature, that I may live eternally!

36.12.10.en: O the overflow of Your tenderness!

36.12.11.en: You forgive me my sins and my disobedience, You take away my uncleannesses and give me the holy life!

36.12.12.en: As for me, I always remember my weakness, and confess to You Your favor upon me!

36.12.13.en: Make me, O Lord, a holy mountain for You!
